metadata.name: WordPress Core Execution Tests - HTML API
metadata.description: Code generation tasks for the WordPress HTML API (Tag Processor, HTML Processor, and decoder)

tests.prompt: Implement a function that hardens the outbound links in a chunk of HTML. Every anchor whose URL points at a host other than this WordPress site must carry rel="noopener". Anchors pointing at this site, root-relative links, fragment-only links and mailto: links must come back exactly as they were, and an anchor that already carries a rel value must keep its existing tokens with noopener appended after a single space. Rewrite the markup with the WordPress HTML API rather than with regular expressions.
tests.expected_behavior: The function walks the anchors with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`, resolves each `href` to a host with `wp_parse_url()`, and only touches anchors whose host is present and differs from the host of `home_url()`. A URL without a host component (relative, fragment, `mailto:`) is off-limits. An existing `rel` is preserved and `noopener` appended; markup without anchors round-trips byte-for-byte through `get_updated_html()`.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API to read and update the anchors
Treat only anchors whose URL carries a host different from this site's as off-site
Append noopener to an existing rel value, separated by one space, instead of replacing it
Return the markup unchanged when there is nothing to harden

tests.prompt: Implement a function that marks up site navigation. Add the CSS class wpbp-crumb to every anchor that appears anywhere inside a <nav> element, however deeply it is nested, and leave every anchor outside a <nav> untouched. Classes an anchor already carries must be preserved.
tests.expected_behavior: The function parses the fragment with `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` (whose only supported context is `<body>`) and decides per anchor from the full element path returned by `get_breadcrumbs()`, so an anchor nested in `nav > ul > li > a` matches just as a direct `nav > a` child does. A `matches_breadcrumbs( array( 'NAV', 'A' ) )` test only catches direct children and misses the nested anchors.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API's document-aware processor so element nesting is known
Match anchors at any depth inside a nav element, not only direct children
Add the class without discarding classes the anchor already has
Return the updated markup

tests.prompt: Implement a function that relabels a call to action: replace the visible text of the first <button> in the supplied markup with the supplied replacement text and return the document. The replacement is plain text supplied by a site editor, so any HTML-significant characters in it must end up encoded rather than parsed as markup. Everything else in the document, including the button's own attributes and their original quoting, must come back byte for byte, and markup without a button must round-trip unchanged.
tests.expected_behavior: The function finds the first `BUTTON` with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::next_tag()`, advances to the element's text with `next_token()`, and writes the replacement with `set_modifiable_text()`, which performs the HTML encoding itself (`<`, `>`, `&`, `"` and `'` become character references, the apostrophe as `'`). Only the first button changes; the rest of the byte stream, including single-quoted attribute values, is preserved because only a lexical text update is queued.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API to locate the button and rewrite its text
Pass the replacement through as plain, unescaped text and let the HTML API encode it
Change only the first button and leave every other byte of the document alone
Return the markup unchanged when there is no button

required_patterns.description: Rewrites the text through the HTML API
Advances to the element's text token

tests.prompt: Implement a function that builds a document outline from a chunk of post content. Return one entry per heading, in document order, as an array with the key 'level' holding the heading level 1-6 as an integer, 'text' holding the heading's readable text with character references decoded and any inline markup inside it stripped, and 'id' holding the heading's id attribute or an empty string when it has none. Read the document with the WordPress HTML API rather than with regular expressions.
tests.expected_behavior: The function scans every token with `next_token()`, opens an entry on an `H1`-`H6` opener (recording the level and `get_attribute( 'id' )`), accumulates `get_modifiable_text()` from the `#text` tokens it then encounters (so text split by inline elements such as `EM` is joined and `&` is decoded to `&`), and closes the entry on the matching heading closer. Nested headings inside sections and headings without an id are handled the same way.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API to walk the document
Return a list of arrays with the keys level, text and id
Report the level as an integer and the missing id as an empty string
Join heading text that is interrupted by inline elements and decode character references

required_patterns.description: Walks every token, not only tags
Reads decoded text through the HTML API

tests.prompt: Implement a function that applies a site's lazy-loading policy to a chunk of HTML: give loading="lazy" to each that does not already declare a loading attribute of any kind, and skip every image that sits inside a element because the browser picks the source there. Images that already declare loading, including the valueless form , must be returned untouched.
tests.expected_behavior: The function uses `WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment()` so `get_breadcrumbs()` can reveal a `PICTURE` ancestor, and treats an image as already configured whenever `get_attribute( 'loading' )` is not `null` -- a valueless attribute reads back as boolean `true`, so a check such as `is_string()` or `empty()` wrongly re-adds the attribute to ``.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API's document-aware processor so ancestors are known
Skip images that appear anywhere inside a picture element
Treat a valueless loading attribute as already declared
Return the updated markup

tests.prompt: Implement a function that improves image accessibility in post content: inside each <figure> that has both a <figcaption> and an image with no alt attribute at all, copy the caption's readable text into that image's alt attribute. An image that already declares alt keeps its value, including when the declared value is the empty string, and a figure without a caption is left alone. The caption may appear before or after the image.
tests.expected_behavior: The function scans tokens with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor`, marks a candidate image with `set_bookmark()`, collects the caption text from the `#text` tokens inside `FIGCAPTION`, and at the figure's closer uses `seek()` to move backwards to the bookmarked image, writes `alt`, then seeks forward again to continue. `get_attribute( 'alt' )` returns `''` for `alt=""` and `null` only when the attribute is absent, so an `empty()` test wrongly overwrites a deliberate empty alt.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API, including its bookmark and seek support, to revisit the image
Only fill alt when the image declares no alt attribute at all
Handle a caption that appears either before or after the image in the same figure
Return the updated markup

required_patterns.description: Seeks back to the bookmarked image
Reads the caption text through the HTML API

tests.prompt: Implement a function that sanitizes untrusted HTML before it is echoed: strip the style attribute and every inline event-handler attribute (any attribute whose name starts with "on") from every element, whatever case they were written in, and keep every other attribute exactly as it was, including data-style and data-onclick. tests.expected_behavior: The function walks every tag with `WP_HTML_Tag_Processor::next_tag()`, calls `remove_attribute( 'style' )` (which matches attribute names case-insensitively) and removes each name reported by `get_attribute_names_with_prefix( 'on' )`, which returns the lowercased names of attributes with that prefix and therefore excludes `data-onclick`.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API to inspect and remove attributes
Remove the style attribute and every attribute whose name begins with on, regardless of the case it was written in
Leave data- attributes and all other attributes untouched
Return the sanitized markup

tests.prompt: Implement a function that audits the comment nodes in a chunk of post content so an editor can find stray notes. Return, in document order, one entry per comment node that is not a WordPress block delimiter: an array with 'type' holding the token type WordPress reports for it, 'comment_type' holding the kind of syntax that produced the comment (null when WordPress reports none) and 'text' holding the whole comment content as a browser would see it, not just the part that may be edited. Block delimiter comments, whose content starts with " wp:" or " /wp:", are skipped, and tokens that are not comments must not appear at all.
tests.expected_behavior: The function walks tokens with `next_token()` and keeps only `#comment` and `#funky-comment` tokens, reporting `get_token_type()`, `get_comment_type()` and `get_full_comment_text()`. The full text differs from the modifiable text for the invalid-syntax forms: a CDATA lookalike reports `[CDATA[...]]` and an XML declaration reports `?xml ...?`. A processing instruction such as `<?wp-bit {...}?>` is its own `#processing-instruction` token in WordPress 7.1 and is not a comment, so it is excluded.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API to walk every token
Report the token type, the comment type and the full browser-visible comment text
Skip WordPress block delimiter comments
Include only comment tokens, funky comments included

tests.prompt: Implement a function that screens link targets for script URLs. It is given the raw text of an href attribute exactly as it appears in an HTML source document, before any decoding, and must report whether a browser would read that value as a javascript: URL. The scheme comparison ignores ASCII case, and the value may hide the scheme behind HTML character references, including ones written without a trailing semicolon. Use the WordPress HTML API's decoding support so the attribute-context rules are applied rather than generic entity decoding.
tests.expected_behavior: The function calls `WP_HTML_Decoder::attribute_starts_with( $raw, 'javascript:', 'ascii-case-insensitive' )`, which compares the decoded prefix without allocating the whole decoded string and applies the attribute-context rules: numeric references decode even without a semicolon (`&#106avascript:`), while a named reference without a semicolon followed by `=` or an ASCII alphanumeric stays literal (`&colon=`), which `html_entity_decode()` and a plain prefix test both get wrong.
requirements: Use the WordPress HTML API's attribute decoding support
Compare the scheme without regard to ASCII case
Treat the input as raw, undecoded attribute text
Return a boolean
